name: Oriana Power Ltd
tagline: Solar EPC/RESCO developer on SME board with a 60,000 TPA SECI green-ammonia offtake contract (~Rs 3,135 Cr/10-yr revenue), but governance red flags (SEBI warning letter, ~1/3 related-party historic revenue) and trusted-user balance-sheet distrust keep conviction LOW despite 10x-eligible headline math.
business_overview: Oriana Power Ltd is a solar EPC (engineering, procurement, construction) and RESCO (renewable energy supply company; build-own-operate) developer listed on the SME board of NSE. The company has diversified into battery energy storage systems (BESS), green hydrogen/ammonia, compressed biogas (CBG) and e-fuels. Historically, solar EPC/RESCO was the core revenue driver; approximately 1/3 of historic revenue came from sales to promoter-affiliated entities. The March 2026 formalisation of a SECI green-ammonia purchase agreement (PA) marks a transition to a large, arm's-length revenue stream: 60,000 TPA at Rs 52.25/kg over 10 years, project sited at Sagar (Madhya Pradesh), end off-taker Madhya Bharat Agro, estimated ~Rs 3,135 Cr total contract value (~Rs 300 Cr/yr average once operational). The project was originally awarded via a SIGHT (Strategic Importance of Green Hydrogen and Fuel Transitions) LoA in August 2025.

fundamentals_narrative: Oriana Power's headline metrics (reported ROCE ~32%, revenue growth ~159% YoY off a small base) arithmetically qualify for a 10x-in-2-3-years thesis. However, the numbers rest on two critical uncertainties: (1) model integrity and (2) execution risk. Model integrity is compromised by a March 2025 SEBI warning letter (still unresolved) and the fact that ~1/3 of historic revenue was sales to promoter-affiliated entities, making independent verification of profitability difficult from outside. Execution risk is substantial: the green-ammonia plant is years away (FY27-FY28 commissioning target), capital-intensive (~Rs 3,135 Cr contract value implies similar capex footprint), and contingent on the company successfully deploying yet-unproven technology and process know-how. Management's diversification into BESS, CBG, and e-fuels adds optionality but spreads resources and delays focus. The SECI green-ammonia PA is materially positive — it is the company's first large, arm's-length, contracted revenue stream with visible off-taker credit (SECI's purchasing agreement, end-buyer Madhya Bharat Agro) — but does not resolve the governance overhang or provide near-term revenue catalyst. For a 10x thesis to hold, three conditions must concurrently hold: (1) the SEBI matter must clear cleanly; (2) the company must successfully construct and commission the green-ammonia plant on time and within cost; (3) the plant must operate at stated capacity and margins without major unplanned capex. The probability of all three is LOW.

verdict_headline: SECI green-ammonia PA is a real, long-term revenue catalyst, but HIGH CAUTION governance red flags, unproven execution, and low moat keep conviction LOW. A 10x is arithmetically plausible if all bets land, but the probability is below 25%.
verdict_reasoning: Governance and model integrity are the gate. The March 2025 SEBI warning letter and ~1/3 related-party historic revenue make the reported ROCE and profit base unverifiable from outside. Multiple elevated-tier users distrust the balance sheet. Until the SEBI matter is formally resolved and related-party revenue is clearly de-emphasised, the investment case cannot be credibly stress-tested.

The SECI green-ammonia PA is genuinely positive and is the company's first large, arm's-length revenue stream. However, revenue is years away (FY27-FY28 commissioning), depends on flawless execution of a plant Oriana has never built, and carries execution risk in a nascent technology domain.

Thesis fit: 10x-in-2-3-years is arithmetically supported (if ROCE stays at 32% and revenue grows at current 159% rate for 2-3 years, a 10x is possible), but execution risk is very high and governance concerns make the model unreliable. The probability of realising a 10x in the 2-3-year window is below 25% in a base case.
